advances: Actual common closed cap in a one-base ambient simplex. Slicing and summing are done on the original integer bases.

proof:
The two sums $\sum_{i\in I}\delta_i\lambda_i$ and $\sum_{j\in J}\delta_j\lambda_j$ agree at height $s$. Normalizing the summands in each group recovers $\alpha,\beta$ from a section point, and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$ gives the common sum $1/L$. This proves the parametrization. Multiplying the affine cap inequality by the positive $L$ gives the stated linear condition.

To compute the slice measure, take positive coordinates $x_i$ in the full orthant, and set $S=\sum_i x_i$ and $D=\sum_i(h_i-s)x_i$. The change $x_i=S\lambda_i$ has Jacobian $S^{m}$ for independent barycentrics, and $D=S(\sum_i h_i\lambda_i-s)$. Thus at $S=1,D=0$ the coordinate disintegration of $dx$ in $(S,D)$ is precisely the barycentric disintegration at height $s$. Mapping barycentrics to $C$ multiplies ordinary coordinate volume by $m!V$, and the coarea factor for the Euclidean first coordinate is one.

In the orthant first rescale each $x_i$ by $\delta_i$. Write the rescaled coordinates as $u\alpha$ on $I$ and $v\beta$ on $J$, so $D=v-u$ and $S=u\sum_{i\in I}\alpha_i/\delta_i+v\sum_{j\in J}\beta_j/\delta_j$. The absolute Jacobian from $(u,v)$ to $(S,D)$ is $L$. The factor for the two radial substitutions is $u^{|I|-1}v^{|J|-1}$, and for the diagonal rescaling it is $(\prod_i\delta_i)^{-1}$. Evaluating at $S=1,D=0$ gives $u=v=1/L$, hence the resulting factor $L^{-(|I|+|J|-1)}=L^{-m}$. These are ordinary changes of variables with nonzero determinants, which give the disintegration identity by integrating against test functions of $(S,D)$. The resulting integrals are continuous at the evaluated level for a cap with nonzero continuous normal by dominated convergence, as the equality set of its affine constraint on the limiting slice is volume-null. For a vertical cap the entire slice is taken or excluded directly by the closed indicator. Thus the formula gives actual slice mass, including a vertical equality even if an a.e. disintegration does not specify it.

For interior knots and endpoints, the convex fibers converge in Hausdorff distance by compactness and convex interpolation from an interior height on the approached side. Their indicators converge almost everywhere, and for a nonvertical cut its boundary in the continuous coordinates has volume zero. Dominated convergence gives the asserted limits for its cut volume. For a vertical cut the closed base indicator gives the exact value. Finite summation gives the mixed cap mass.
